title: Orphan BTC: real Stratum Bitcoin miner in the FPGA
summary: A real Bitcoin miner on the S9 control board's FPGA: 4 double-SHA-256 units (about 1.1 MH/s) driven by a Stratum v1 pool client on the ARM, every result re-checked against the pool's exact share target. Built on Ardzy's 13_sha256 lab (by chryso, GPL-3.0). At this speed it is a lottery miner for solo pools such as public-pool.io. Includes a 3 % opt-out dev fee and fan control. by JMSCNC, makers of RotatoCAM.
quickstart: Load orphan_btc. Its page opens on port 8000.
Enter your Bitcoin address; the pool defaults to the solo pool public-pool.io (difficulty 0.001).
Save, then Start mining. The log shows jobs, shares sent and the pool's answers.
3 % dev fee is on by default (3 of every 100 minutes to the developer); untick it to opt out.
Fans: Cooling in the Orphan menu.

slots.1: SHA-256 miner (Ardzy's sha_miner: 4 units, midstate + tail, zero-bit target)
slots.5: LED scanner (orphan_larson): the 4 LEDs breathe in a slow scanner while mining
